page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and a bundled 1919 GB local SSD storage volume. Network connectivity is supported by a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with the stress-ng multi-core test and Geekbench multi-core score both landing in the middle 50% tier. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom 25% results in stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier, reaching 51.37 GB/sec for large block reads and 41.05 GB/sec for writes. Database operations, such as Redis SET, perform in the bottom 25%, while static web serving throughput is average at 6.68 GB/sec. LLM inference on a medium 7B model is poor, though small 135M model processing is average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i3.2xlarge offers a high density of local SSD storage paired with a generous memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a viable option for storage-heavy workloads without the premium of specialized bare-metal hardware. The tradeoff lies in its modest single-core CPU performance. This server is best suited for local database hosting, caching layers, static web serving, and general-purpose storage-intensive applications that benefit from large local SSD capacity and moderate memory overhead.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.2xlarge is an x86_64 server featuring an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 1919 GB local SSD. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark data shows average multi-core CPU and memory performance, though single-core execution and Redis SET operations fall into the weaker tiers. With its high local storage capacity and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-heavy deployments. It is well-suited for localized databases, static web serving, and memory-reliant storage workloads.
